sources.title: Book of the Dead
sources.author: Ancient Egyptian priests
sources.excerpt: I have not done evil to mankind. I have not oppressed the members of my family.
sources.longExcerpt: I have not done evil to mankind. I have not oppressed the members of my family. This historical source from -1550 provides valuable insight into the sub-saharan-africa region during the antiquity period. It represents the voices, experiences, and perspectives of people who lived during this transformative time in human history. Such primary sources are essential for understanding not just the major events of history, but the daily lives, beliefs, and struggles of ordinary people across different cultures and time periods.

sources.title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
sources.author: Unknown Greek merchant
sources.excerpt: Beyond Opone, the coast trending more to the south, come the Small and Great Bluffs of Azania. After about four thousand stadia sailing along the Azanian coast, there is the island Menuthias, about three hundred stadia from the mainland, low and wooded.
sources.longExcerpt: Beyond Opone, the coast trending more to the south, come the Small and Great Bluffs of Azania. After about four thousand stadia sailing along the Azanian coast, there is the island Menuthias, about three hundred stadia from the mainland, low and wooded. The inhabitants of this coast are men of piratical habits, very tall, and under separate chiefs for each place. This ancient trading manual from 60 CE provides invaluable insight into East African trade, describing the ports, peoples, and products of the ancient African coast from Egypt to Tanzania.

sources.title: The Voyage of Hanno
sources.author: Hanno the Navigator
sources.excerpt: We passed a country burning with fires and perfumes; and streams of fire supplied from it fell into the sea. The country was impassable on account of the heat.
sources.longExcerpt: We passed a country burning with fires and perfumes; and streams of fire supplied from it fell into the sea. The country was impassable on account of the heat. We sailed quickly thence, being much terrified; and passing on for four days, we discovered at night a country full of fire. This Carthaginian account from 500 BCE describes one of the earliest known explorations of the West African coast, possibly reaching as far as Mount Cameroon with its active volcanic activity.
